newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle market at standstill - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle market at standstill - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade near midday Monday remained at a standstill, with no sales of slaughter steers or heifers and few bids reported, feedlot sources said.
A few bids of $69.00 to $70.00 per cwt were reported, with owners asking $71.00 to mostly $72.00, they said.
Prices were expected to be supported by ongoing tight numbers of finished cattle on showlists. Overall, showlists were running shorter than last week, sources said.
The Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma list was seen down about 11,000 head near 54,000, sources there said.
Light support also was tied to last week's moderately active beef movement, the sources said.
However, if beef demand starts drying up, it could have a negative impact on fed cattle prices despite tight feedlot supplies, said Dave Maher, livestock analyst with Securities Corp. of Iowa.
"Right now we're working off of last week, which looked pretty good," Maher said.
Beef prices at midday Monday were quoted down $0.27 to up $0.56 per cwt on 57 fabricated loads sold, according to USDA.
